objective: Add the Revision D mobile bimanual robot description called for by Issue #327 as a separate model under robot/description/revision_d/: base, four steer-drive modules, braked lift, torso, head/neck, tool dock, sensors and two seven-axis arms, with exactly 14 named revolute manipulator joints, collision geometry on every solid body, a deterministic single-rooted TF tree, a fail-closed ros2_control declaration behind sim_gz:=true, a Gazebo spawn launch, checkers that compare the model against hardware/mechanical/design-spec.json, a generated frame artifact, frame/joint documentation and a migration note, while leaving robot/description/workbench.urdf.xacro byte-for-byte unchanged.
decision_supported: Whether the repository has a truthful, machine-checked Gazebo/ROS description for the Revision D product configuration, without inventing physical evidence, without altering the frozen tabletop fixture, and without duplicating ownership of the arm, navigation, camera-collision or device-runtime boundaries owned by #260, #152, #261 and #230.
acceptance: the model declares explicit links, inertials, collisions and frames for the base, the four steer-drive modules, the lift, the torso, the head/neck, the tool dock, the sensors and both arms, and validate_description.py asserts each of those frames exists

the model contains exactly 14 named revolute manipulator joints with limits taken from design-spec.json#/manipulator/joints, and the wheel steering, wheel drive, neck and lift joints are modelled separately by type so they cannot be counted as manipulator axes

the chassis width, depth, wheelbase, track, wheel diameter, ground clearance, base-top height, stowed torso bottom, minimum and maximum shoulder height, stowed head top, shoulder spacing, arm link lengths and joint limits are sourced from hardware/mechanical/design-spec.json, and any divergence fails validation unless it is listed with a reason in known_divergences

the TF tree is deterministic and complete with exactly one root (map) covering odom/base_link, lift, torso, head, both arm chains, the tool frames and the sensor optical frames, with the REP-103 optical convention and the base axis convention documented in FRAMES.md

every solid body carries exactly one collision primitive matching its visual primitive, convention frames carry none, and validation fails on a visual-only primitive or on a link that would read as free space to the planner

ros2_control is opt-in behind sim_gz:=true, declares named controllers only, exposes no whole-body joint group or unguarded trajectory path to the lift, and the Gazebo launch refuses to start without a simulator instead of half-starting

the Gazebo acceptance cases required by the issue (spawn, joint-limit rejection, self/forbidden-volume collision, lift states, stabilizer states, clean shutdown and restart) are enumerated and report NOT_EXECUTED, with exit code 2, when no simulator is present, so an unrun case is never rendered as a pass

the deployed stabilizer pad centre lands on the documented stabilized support polygon from design-spec.json#/stability_analysis, and the pads occupy four distinct corners rather than collapsing onto one axis

the tabletop fixture robot/description/workbench.urdf.xacro is unchanged, keeps its world root and its camera_body collision, and no frozen scenario, registry entry, shared contract or Pydantic model is modified

make description-check expands the model, validates it against the mechanical spec and regenerates and diffs the generated frame artifact so a stale or hand-edited artifact fails, and the artifact is byte-identical across two generations of one commit

README.md, FRAMES.md and MIGRATION.md record the hardware and HIL status as NOT_EXECUTED, the physical validation status, the self_collide modelling boundary, and the integration boundary against #260, #152, #261 and #230, without claiming navigation, stability, torque validation or execution authority
evidence: the committed Revision D xacro, control declaration, controller set and launch file in robot/description/revision_d/
validate_description.py output showing every assertion passes against the expanded model and naming the design-spec pointer for each anchored value
generated/revision-d-frames.json plus a --check run proving the artifact is current and byte-identical across two generations of one commit
gazebo_acceptance.py output showing the required cases as NOT_EXECUTED with exit code 2 when no simulator is present
the focused pytest run for tests/unit/test_revision_d_description.py and tests/unit/test_revision_d_gazebo.py, including the mutation test that a diverged lift travel fails validation
full-suite pytest output with passed and skipped counts, ruff check and ruff format output, mkdocs build --strict output, make context-check output and git diff --check output
stop_conditions: the change would require editing robot/description/workbench.urdf.xacro or any frozen scenario, registry entry, golden set or shared contract
the change would require writing robot/control/, firmware/, hardware/, kernel/ or bsp/
the change would require a two-way coupling with navigation (#152), the MoveIt bridge (#260), the device runtime (#230) or camera collision #261 instead of a documented boundary
the change would require amending interfaces/ or libs/contracts/, which needs three independent human approvals
the change would require a Gazebo, HIL or physical run to be reported as passing, or any NOT_EXECUTED case to be converted into a pass
the change would require claiming navigation, localization, stability or validated arm torque from the model
a required modification falls outside allowed_paths
data_classification: public repository source and documentation only; no secrets, personal data, credentials or physical measurement data
model_policy: AI may write the description, the local checkers, the generated frame artifact and the tests from the committed mechanical spec and the existing tabletop fixture; a named human Motion Owner accepts the model, the frame conventions, the joint limits and the integration boundaries it fixes, and no AI output in this packet constitutes a physical or safety result
risks_and_fallbacks: the model could be read as a claim that the Revision D robot has been built or validated; fallback is that hardware and HIL status are NOT_EXECUTED, validation_status stays CONCEPT_PHYSICAL_VALIDATION_REQUIRED, and README.md states the boundary explicitly

the stabilizer mechanism could be read as a stability result; fallback is that stability_gates.analytical_screen_only is true, the required physical tests are listed as unrun, and drive_tip_angle_is_not_manipulation_release still holds

a derived residual such as the neck standoff or the stabilizer stroke could drift from the documented value it preserves; fallback is that validate_description.py asserts the documented end value, not the residual, and the divergence list fails on anything unexplained
self_collide being false could be read as a safety statement; fallback is that FRAMES.md and README.md record it as a modelling limitation owned by the forbidden-volume and contact tests

the Revision D controllers could be read as an execution path for the lift; fallback is that the lift is reachable only through a named trajectory controller, no whole-body joint group exists, and STOP/safe-stop authority stays with Motion and the safety controller
the generated artifact could be edited by hand or go stale; fallback is that make description-check regenerates and diffs it, and the unit test compares it against a fresh in-process generation
rollback is a revert of this commit; the change is additive and touches no runtime, fixture, contract, dependency or protected module
